key_insight: Across a broad parameter sweep, mobile ions have only a small effect on steady-state performance in efficient perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Design efforts should prioritize key device parameters such as recombination, ion density, and band offsets, since these dominate performance more than ion mobility in well-optimized cells.
method: Drift-diffusion simulations of perovskite solar cells
Factorial analysis across ion density, recombination rate, and band offsets
Paired comparison of 601 ion-enabled devices against identical ion-free controls
evidence_signal: The study simulated 601 device pairs, or 1202 total cells, spanning physically relevant materials parameters for n-i-p and p-i-n architectures with different contact layers.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on modeled steady-state behavior, so transient effects and real-device degradation mechanisms may still alter the practical impact of mobile ions.
paper_title: An Investigation into the Effect of Mobile Ions on the Steady State Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
